title: Covariant canonical-spinor amplitudes for partial wave analysis
summary: We propose a covariant orbital-spin ($LS$) decomposed amplitude for the partial wave analysis using the massive spinor-helicity formalism. First we review the traditional-$LS$ method in the little group space and the Zemach tensor method in the double cover of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ space. To recover the $\mathrm{SO}(3,1)$ Lorentz covariance, several Lorentz covariant $LS$ tensors have been constructed in several different methods: covariant tensor, covariant projection tensor in pure-spin and general-spin schemes, but performing a intrinsic separation between $LS$ coupling while maintaining covariance is not obvious. We utilize the massive canonical-spinor variables to determine general three-point amplitudes, in which the spin-orbital decomposition is realized in single little group space by projecting little group indices of each particles into one, while the Lorentz covariance is ensured by the spinor form naturally. This covariant spinor method allows direct evaluation in any frame and a streamlined treatment of cascade decays within a single frame without additional alignment rotations in non-covariant treatment. As a benchmark, we implement the method in TF-PWA and analyze $Λ_c^+\toΛπ^+π^0$, finding consistent fit results across the helicity, traditional-$LS$, and canonical-spinor amplitudes. This validates the canonical-spinor amplitude as a practical tool for modern partial wave analyses of complex decay chains.

AI.tldr: Proposes a covariant orbital-spin (LS) decomposed amplitude for partial wave analysis using massive spinor-helicity formalism, enabling Lorentz-covariant LS separation without frame-dependent rotations.
AI.motivation: Traditional LS methods lack Lorentz covariance, requiring frame-dependent rotations for cascade decays. Existing covariant approaches don't provide intrinsic LS separation while maintaining covariance.
AI.method: Uses massive canonical-spinor variables to construct three-point amplitudes with LS decomposition in single little group space, projecting little group indices into one while maintaining Lorentz covariance through spinor form.
AI.result: Implemented in TF-PWA and tested on Λc⁺→Λπ⁺π⁰ decay, finding consistent fit results across helicity, traditional-LS, and canonical-spinor amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: Canonical-spinor amplitude provides a practical, covariant tool for modern partial wave analyses of complex decay chains, enabling direct evaluation in any frame without additional alignment rotations.

title: Domain Walls from $Σ(36 \times 3)$, $Δ(54)$ and $Δ(27)$ potentials
summary: We consider the degenerate minima arising from scalar potentials invariant under $Σ(36\times 3)$, or under its subgroups $Δ(54)$ and $Δ(27)$ (with or without imposed CP symmetries), for a triplet of those symmetries. In this framework, we classify the distinct Domain Walls between the degenerate minima and calculate the respective tensions.

AI.tldr: Classification and tension calculation of domain walls in scalar potentials with Σ(36×3), Δ(54), and Δ(27) symmetries for triplet representations.
AI.motivation: Study degenerate minima in scalar potentials with discrete non-Abelian symmetries (Σ(36×3), Δ(54), Δ(27)) to understand domain wall formation and properties in such symmetric systems.
AI.method: Analyze scalar potentials invariant under specified discrete symmetries for triplet representations, classify distinct domain walls between degenerate minima, and calculate their tensions using field theory methods.
AI.result: Complete classification of distinct domain walls for each symmetry group, with calculated tensions for each type of domain wall configuration.
AI.conclusion: Provides systematic understanding of domain wall structures in systems with Σ(36×3), Δ(54), and Δ(27) symmetries, with implications for cosmology and symmetry breaking patterns.

title: Momentum fraction and hard scale dependence of double parton scattering in heavy-ion collisions
summary: In a previous work, we studied the momentum fraction and hard--scale dependence of double parton scattering (DPS) in proton--proton collisions and the resulting dependence of the effective cross section on the final--state observables. In this paper, we extend those results to heavy--ion ($pA$ and $AA$) collisions, accounting for nuclear effects in the relevant kinematic region, namely shadowing and antishadowing. In addition to modifying the longitudinal parton distributions, these effects also alter the transverse parton distribution of the nucleus, for which we propose a simple model. We further hypothesize that partons inside a bound nucleon are more widely separated than in a free proton. We compute the effective cross section for the available $p$Pb data, obtaining reasonable agreement, and provide predictions for future measurements at the LHC. The observed dependence of our predictions on the final state indicates that DPS in heavy--ion collisions can be used to probe the transverse profile of the free proton and the bound nucleon, primarily in $pA$ collisions, as well as the transverse structure of the nucleus, mainly in $AA$ collisions.

AI.tldr: Extends double parton scattering (DPS) analysis from pp to heavy-ion collisions (pA, AA), incorporating nuclear effects like shadowing/antishadowing and proposing a model for transverse parton distribution modifications in nuclei.
AI.motivation: To extend previous DPS studies from proton-proton collisions to heavy-ion collisions (pA and AA), accounting for nuclear effects that modify both longitudinal and transverse parton distributions, and to test hypotheses about differences between bound and free nucleons.
AI.method: Extends previous DPS framework to heavy-ion collisions, incorporates nuclear effects (shadowing, antishadowing), proposes a simple model for transverse parton distribution modifications in nuclei, hypothesizes wider parton separation in bound nucleons, and computes effective cross sections for available pPb data.
AI.result: Obtains reasonable agreement with available pPb data for effective cross section calculations, provides predictions for future LHC measurements, and demonstrates that DPS in heavy-ion collisions can probe transverse structure of protons, bound nucleons, and nuclei.
AI.conclusion: DPS in heavy-ion collisions serves as a valuable probe of transverse structure: pA collisions primarily probe transverse profiles of free protons and bound nucleons, while AA collisions mainly probe transverse structure of nuclei, with predictions provided for future LHC measurements.

title: Improved supernova bounds on CP-even scalars: cooling and decay constraints
summary: Supernovae provide among the most powerful probes of weakly-coupled new particles in the MeV mass range, where laboratory experiments lose sensitivity. In this work, we derive improved supernova constraints on CP-even scalars mixing with the Higgs boson, combining an updated production rate calculation, which improves the cooling bound by more than an order of magnitude, with new decay-based constraints from the galactic 511~keV positron flux and energy deposition in low-energy Type~II-P supernovae. Together, these constraints probe mixing angles as small as $\sinθ\sim 10^{-9}$, more than five orders of magnitude below existing collider bounds. We also extend our analysis to a hadrophilic scalar model, constraining Yukawa couplings down to $y_N \sim 10^{-10}$. Our results demonstrate that the combination of astrophysical and collider probes covers over nine orders of magnitude in coupling for these classes of models, probing a large region of parameter space motivated by dark matter considerations.

AI.tldr: Supernovae provide powerful probes for MeV-scale new particles, with improved constraints on Higgs-mixing scalars and hadrophilic scalars covering nine orders of magnitude in coupling.
AI.motivation: Supernovae offer unique sensitivity to weakly-coupled new particles in the MeV mass range where laboratory experiments lose sensitivity, making them valuable probes for physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Combined updated production rate calculations for improved cooling bounds with new decay-based constraints from galactic 511 keV positron flux and energy deposition in low-energy Type II-P supernovae.
AI.result: Constraints probe mixing angles as small as sinθ ∼ 10⁻⁹ (five orders below collider bounds) and Yukawa couplings down to y_N ∼ 10⁻¹⁰, covering over nine orders of magnitude in coupling.
AI.conclusion: The combination of astrophysical and collider probes provides comprehensive coverage of parameter space for Higgs-mixing and hadrophilic scalar models, particularly relevant for dark matter considerations.

title: Quantum field theories with many fields
summary: The large-$N$ quantum field theories provide a window into the regime of strongly-coupled physics. Our principal object of study in this thesis is the large-$N$ family of melonic QFTs, which contain the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev-like models, tensor models, and vector models. We begin with a review of this limit of a large number of degrees of freedom (large-$N$) as an approach to the solution of QFTs. Two toy models are used to clarify this approach: a zero-dimensional field theory and the flow of a generalized free field theory. Both models are solvable, and so we can explicitly demonstrate: using the former, the simplifications at large $N$; using the latter, the tools used to study scale-dependence of physics -- the renormalization group. We develop $\tilde{F}$-extremization, a simple method of solution for an arbitrary large-$N$ melonic QFT in its strongly-coupled limit. The infrared conformal field theories show remarkable simplicity, in that they are entirely solved by the requirement that they have as many degrees of freedom as possible, up to a simple constraint arising from the interaction between the fields. We measure the number of degrees of freedom of the conformal infrared theory via $\tilde{F}$, the universal part of the free energy. We then present the example of the quartic Yukawa model in continuous dimension. This model is considered as a tensor field theory, and solved for its conformal limit; we then illustrate its multiplicity of fixed points and their stability, as well as its operator spectrum, matching the data between the large-$N$ and dimensional expansions. These features reflect general characteristics of melonic conformal field theories: their existence, stability, and spectral characteristics. We conclude with future directions of exploration for the melonic theories.

AI.tldr: Thesis develops F̃-extremization method to solve large-N melonic QFTs in strong-coupling limit, demonstrating simplicity of infrared CFTs and applying to quartic Yukawa tensor model.
AI.motivation: Large-N quantum field theories provide access to strongly-coupled physics; melonic QFTs (including SYK-like models, tensor models, vector models) are particularly tractable in this limit and offer insights into strongly-coupled regimes.
AI.method: Develops F̃-extremization method for solving arbitrary large-N melonic QFTs in strong-coupling limit; uses zero-dimensional field theory and generalized free field theory as pedagogical examples; applies method to quartic Yukawa tensor model in continuous dimension.
AI.result: Infrared CFTs show remarkable simplicity, solved by maximizing degrees of freedom subject to interaction constraints; quartic Yukawa model exhibits multiple fixed points with stability analysis and operator spectrum matching between large-N and dimensional expansions.
AI.conclusion: Melonic CFTs demonstrate general characteristics of existence, stability, and spectral properties; F̃-extremization provides systematic solution method; future directions for melonic theories exploration are outlined.

title: 50 Years of SUSY and SUGRA, circa 1974-2024, and Future Prospects
summary: The development in the early seventies of supersymmetry, in the mid-seventies of gauge supersymmetry and supergravity, and in the early eighties of gravity mediated breaking of supersymmetry and of supergravity grand unification have led to remarkable progress in the pursuit of unification of fundamental interactions of particle physics. They have also led to the intertwining of particle physics, cosmology, and strings. Since supersymmetry and supergravity are manifest in the low energy limit of superstring below the Planck scale, experimental test of them are of interest regarding the validity of the superstring itself. For that reason, over the past decades, after the advent of supersymmetry and SUGRA models, there have been sustained experimental searches for supersymmetry at colliders, in precision experiments, and in astrophysical and cosmological data. The SUSY and SUGRA models have also had deep impact on theories related to inflation, dark matter, and dark energy. The purpose of this article is to provide a view from the bridge of these developments over the past fifty years circa 1974-2024.

AI.tldr: Historical review of supersymmetry and supergravity developments from 1974-2024, covering their role in unification, connection to superstrings, experimental searches, and impact on cosmology including inflation, dark matter, and dark energy.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive historical perspective on the development of supersymmetry (SUSY) and supergravity (SUGRA) over 50 years (1974-2024), examining their role in unifying fundamental interactions, their connection to superstring theory, and their impact on particle physics, cosmology, and experimental searches.
AI.method: Historical review and analysis of theoretical developments in supersymmetry and supergravity, tracing their evolution from early formulations to modern applications. The paper examines the progression from supersymmetry (early 1970s) to gauge supersymmetry and supergravity (mid-1970s), to gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking and supergravity grand unification (early 1980s), and their experimental implications.
AI.result: The paper documents how supersymmetry and supergravity have fundamentally transformed theoretical physics by: 1) Enabling progress toward unification of fundamental interactions, 2) Creating deep connections between particle physics, cosmology, and string theory, 3) Motivating sustained experimental searches at colliders, precision experiments, and astrophysical observations, 4) Influencing theories of inflation, dark matter, and dark energy, 5) Providing a low-energy manifestation of superstring theory below the Planck scale.
AI.conclusion: Supersymmetry and supergravity represent foundational developments in theoretical physics over the past 50 years, serving as crucial bridges between particle physics, cosmology, and string theory. Their experimental verification remains important for validating superstring theory, and they continue to shape research directions in fundamental physics, cosmology, and the search for unification of fundamental forces.

title: Higher-Spin and Higher-Point Constraints on Stringy Amplitudes
summary: We employ multiparticle factorization to constrain deformations of tree-level open string amplitudes. Assuming minimal degeneracy among intermediate states of the same spin up through the second excited level, we find that the Regge intercept among all amplitudes of the Koba-Nielsen type can be uniquely fixed using seven-point factorization, precisely matching the bosonic string. Moreover, we produce novel constraints on deformations of the worldsheet integrand. We then turn to deformations of superstrings, with massless external states and arbitrary spectral degeneracy, using soft kinematics. Accounting for the infinite tower of higher-spin resonances, we obtain novel multipositivity bounds to leading and subleading order in the large-level limit. We apply these bounds to the simplest factorizable satellite deformation in the family of amplitudes found by Gross, showing that any deformation of four-point string amplitudes of this type is forbidden by unitarity. Our results reinforce the folklore that the higher-spin tower of string excitations is dramatically more rigid than any finite number of species.

AI.tldr: The paper uses multiparticle factorization and soft kinematics to constrain deformations of tree-level open string amplitudes, showing that Regge intercepts are uniquely fixed to match bosonic strings and that certain deformations are forbidden by unitarity.
AI.motivation: To understand the rigidity of string theory amplitudes and constrain possible deformations, particularly examining how the infinite tower of higher-spin excitations imposes stronger constraints than finite particle species.
AI.method: Uses multiparticle factorization for bosonic strings with minimal degeneracy assumptions, and soft kinematics for superstrings with arbitrary spectral degeneracy. Applies these techniques to analyze deformations of Koba-Nielsen type amplitudes and Gross's factorizable satellite deformations.
AI.result: 1) Regge intercept for all Koba-Nielsen type amplitudes is uniquely fixed to match bosonic strings using seven-point factorization. 2) Novel constraints on worldsheet integrand deformations. 3) Multipositivity bounds from infinite higher-spin resonances in superstrings. 4) Deformations of four-point string amplitudes in Gross's family are forbidden by unitarity.
AI.conclusion: The infinite tower of higher-spin string excitations imposes dramatically stronger constraints than any finite number of particle species, reinforcing the rigidity of string theory amplitudes against deformations.

title: The effect of charm quark on the QCD chiral phase diagram
summary: We study the influence of charm quark dynamics on the chiral phase structure of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) using the recently developed miniDSE scheme of the Dyson-Schwinger equations. By calculating the quark propagator in $2+1$ and $2+1+1$ flavor QCD, we quantify the impact of including the charm quark as a dynamical degree of freedom on the QCD phase diagram. Our results show that the charm quark induces a moderate but noticeable shift to lower chemical potential in the location of the critical endpoint (CEP) by approximately 2-3%. The result in this work indicates that the heavy-flavor dynamics can subtly influence the QCD phase structure and should be taken into account in particular for searching the CEP of QCD.

AI.tldr: Charm quark dynamics moderately shift QCD critical endpoint to lower chemical potential by 2-3% when included as dynamical degree of freedom.
AI.motivation: To understand how charm quark dynamics influence the chiral phase structure of QCD, particularly the location of the critical endpoint, using advanced computational methods.
AI.method: Employ miniDSE scheme of Dyson-Schwinger equations to calculate quark propagator in both 2+1 flavor (u,d,s) and 2+1+1 flavor (u,d,s,c) QCD configurations.
AI.result: Inclusion of dynamical charm quark induces moderate but noticeable shift of critical endpoint to lower chemical potential by approximately 2-3% compared to 2+1 flavor calculations.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-flavor dynamics subtly influence QCD phase structure and should be accounted for in searches for the critical endpoint, despite relatively small quantitative effect.

title: Nonabelian Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture and Monopole Confinement
summary: Within the known landscape of quantum gravity, most theories satisfy the Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture (LWGC), which requires a superextremal particle at every site in the electric charge lattice $Γ$. However, counterexamples to the LWGC exist, and it was recently hypothesized that such counterexamples necessarily feature fractionally charged confined monopoles. In this work, we verify this hypothesis in toroidal orbifold compactifications of the heterotic string, which notably feature LWGC violation in both the abelian and nonabelian gauge sectors. In all the cases we consider, there exists a discrete subgroup of the center of the gauge group $K \subseteq Z(G)$ such that superextremal particles exist at every site in the charge lattice of the quotient group $G/K$, while (confined) monopoles exist at all sites in the magnetic charge lattice of $G/K$. This suggests that LWGC violation cannot occur for gauge groups with trivial centers, and more generally the degree of LWGC violation in a nonabelian gauge theory is bounded in terms of the maximal order of the center.

AI.tldr: The paper verifies that counterexamples to the Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture (LWGC) in heterotic string compactifications feature fractionally charged confined monopoles, with LWGC violation bounded by the gauge group's center.
AI.motivation: To test the hypothesis that counterexamples to the Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture (LWGC) necessarily involve fractionally charged confined monopoles, particularly in heterotic string compactifications where LWGC violation occurs in both abelian and nonabelian gauge sectors.
AI.method: Analysis of toroidal orbifold compactifications of the heterotic string, examining cases with LWGC violation and studying the relationship between superextremal particles, confined monopoles, and the gauge group's center structure.
AI.result: In all examined cases, there exists a discrete subgroup K of the gauge group's center Z(G) such that: (1) superextremal particles exist at every site in the charge lattice of G/K, and (2) confined monopoles exist at all sites in the magnetic charge lattice of G/K. This suggests LWGC violation cannot occur for gauge groups with trivial centers.
AI.conclusion: The degree of LWGC violation in nonabelian gauge theories is bounded by the maximal order of the gauge group's center, confirming the hypothesis that LWGC counterexamples feature fractionally charged confined monopoles.

title: Exploring Nucleon Structure and the Proton Mass Problem through Holographic QCD
summary: Understanding the internal structure of the proton-including the distributions of quarks and gluons and their contributions to proton properties such as mass-remains a central challenge in quantum chromodynamics (QCD). While quark generalized parton distributions (GPDs) have been studied extensively, a unified approach that simultaneously extracts quark parton distribution functions (PDFs), gravitational form factors (GFFs), and gluon GPDs from experimental constraints is still lacking. Moreover, the role of gluons in proton mass generation, particularly through the trace anomaly mechanism, requires deeper theoretical and phenomenological exploration. In this study, we first extract quark GPDs in protons using parameterization method based on the electromagnetic form factors provided by Light-Front Holographic QCD (LFHQCD) from which we derive both quark PDFs and their GFFs. We then extend this approach to model gluon GPDs. Our calculations show consistency with experimental data and lattice QCD results and successfully reproduce soft Pomeron behavior. Furthermore, we investigate near-threshold $J/ψ$ production using gauge/string duality to quantify the contribution of the trace anomaly to the proton mass. Our results demonstrate that the parameterization method provides a consistent framework for describing both quark and gluon structure, bridging GPDs, PDFs, and GFFs. The analysis of $J/ψ$ production confirms that the trace anomaly contributes significantly ($\sim 23\%$) to the proton mass, with the calculated cross-section dependence on momentum transfer $t$ in agreement with experimental observations. This work advances the understanding of proton structure by integrating quark and gluon degrees of freedom and elucidating the origin of proton mass within QCD.

AI.tldr: Unified extraction of quark PDFs, GFFs, and gluon GPDs from LFHQCD parameterization, with trace anomaly contributing ~23% to proton mass via near-threshold J/ψ production analysis.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of unified approach for simultaneously extracting quark PDFs, gravitational form factors, and gluon GPDs from experimental constraints, and explore gluon contributions to proton mass generation through trace anomaly mechanism.
AI.method: Extract quark GPDs using parameterization method based on electromagnetic form factors from Light-Front Holographic QCD (LFHQCD), derive quark PDFs and GFFs, extend to model gluon GPDs, and investigate near-threshold J/ψ production using gauge/string duality to quantify trace anomaly contribution.
AI.result: Consistency with experimental data and lattice QCD results, successful reproduction of soft Pomeron behavior, parameterization provides consistent framework for describing quark and gluon structure, and trace anomaly contributes ~23% to proton mass with cross-section dependence on momentum transfer t agreeing with experimental observations.
AI.conclusion: The work advances understanding of proton structure by integrating quark and gluon degrees of freedom and elucidating the origin of proton mass within QCD through a unified parameterization framework that bridges GPDs, PDFs, and GFFs.

title: From BPS geodesics to mode-driven dynamics in the scattering of multiple BPS vortices
comment: 18 pages, 16 figures, one video available here: https://youtu.be/o-0fQn-0wlE
summary: We analyze how the geodesic motion in the 3- and 4-vortex sectors of the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling is deformed by the excitation of a massive bound mode. We find that the geodesics corresponding to BPS solutions with enhanced symmetry remain unchanged, although the direction of the actual motion depends on the mode-generated force, i.e., a force arising from the change of the mode frequency along the geodesic. In a generic case, for example in head-on collisions between the axially symmetric 1- and 2-vortex or between two 2-vortices, the vortex trajectories can differ strongly from the BPS geodesic. This enhances the chaotic behavior in the formation of the final state.

AI.tldr: Geodesic motion in 3- and 4-vortex Abelian-Higgs model is deformed by massive bound mode excitation, affecting vortex trajectories and enhancing chaotic behavior in final state formation.
AI.motivation: To understand how the excitation of massive bound modes affects the geodesic motion of vortices in the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, particularly how this deformation influences vortex trajectories and final state formation.
AI.method: Analysis of geodesic motion in 3- and 4-vortex sectors of the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, examining how massive bound mode excitation deforms trajectories, with focus on BPS solutions with enhanced symmetry and generic cases like head-on collisions.
AI.result: Geodesics corresponding to BPS solutions with enhanced symmetry remain unchanged in form, but actual motion direction depends on mode-generated force. In generic cases (head-on collisions between 1- and 2-vortex or two 2-vortices), trajectories differ strongly from BPS geodesics, enhancing chaotic behavior in final state formation.
AI.conclusion: Massive bound mode excitation significantly deforms vortex trajectories from ideal BPS geodesics in most cases, leading to enhanced chaotic dynamics in vortex interactions and final state formation, while preserving the geometric structure of enhanced symmetry BPS solutions.

title: Magnetic moments of strange hidden-bottom pentaquarks and the role of spin flavor correlations
summary: We investigate the magnetic moments of strange hidden bottom pentaquark states within the constituent quark model considering molecular and compact configurations. The system with quark content qqqbb is analyzed in three scenarios a baryon meson molecular configuration bq1bq2q3 a diquark diquark antiquark configuration bq1q2q3b and a diquark triquark configuration bq1bq2q3. The negative parity states with are studied for strangeness. We find that for the dominant spin couplings and maximally aligned configurations the diquark diquark antiquark qqqbb and diquark triquark bqqqb descriptions yield identical or numerically very close magnetic moments indicating that in the hidden bottom sector the magnetic properties are governed primarily by the global spin flavor structure rather than clustering details. A systematic suppression with increasing strangeness and a clear spin hierarchy are observed in all configurations. Due to the large bottom quark mass, heavy quark contributions are strongly suppressed, making the magnetic moments primarily sensitive to light strange spin correlations. These results provide theoretical benchmarks for future experimental studies of exotic multiquark states.

AI.tldr: Magnetic moments of strange hidden-bottom pentaquarks (qqqbb) calculated in constituent quark model for molecular and compact configurations show spin-flavor dominance over clustering details, with heavy quark suppression and light-strange spin correlation sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To investigate magnetic moments of strange hidden-bottom pentaquark states to understand how different structural configurations (molecular vs. compact) affect magnetic properties, and to provide theoretical benchmarks for experimental studies of exotic multiquark states.
AI.method: Constituent quark model analysis of qqqbb systems in three configurations: (1) baryon-meson molecular (bq1bq2q3), (2) diquark-diquark-antiquark (bq1q2q3b), and (3) diquark-triquark (bq1bq2q3). Study negative parity states with strangeness, focusing on dominant spin couplings and maximally aligned configurations.
AI.result: Diquark-diquark-antiquark and diquark-triquark configurations yield identical or numerically very close magnetic moments, indicating magnetic properties are governed by global spin-flavor structure rather than clustering details. Systematic suppression with increasing strangeness and clear spin hierarchy observed. Heavy quark contributions strongly suppressed due to large bottom quark mass, making magnetic moments primarily sensitive to light-strange spin correlations.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic moments of hidden-bottom pentaquarks are determined by global spin-flavor structure rather than specific clustering details, with heavy quark suppression making them sensitive probes of light-strange spin correlations. Results provide theoretical benchmarks for future experimental studies of exotic multiquark states.

title: Spin Chains from large-$N$ QCD at strong coupling
summary: We study the strong coupling expansion of large $N$ QCD in various dimensions, reformulating the Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian on a square lattice in terms of (constrained) one dimensional spin chain models. We study the integrability properties of the spin chain obtained this way: there is large class of integrable subsectors, but we show that the full spin chain is not integrable, at least when viewed from a description based on Bethe ansatz. We demonstrate that the spin chains no longer possess integrability due to the constraints arising from the zigzag symmetry of the confining strings. The spin chain description properly estimates the roughening transition point by extrapolating the first-order analytical results based on integrability of some subsectors. The generalization to higher dimensions are also considered, where we also find the small subsectors without the zigzag constraints to be integrable.

AI.tldr: Large N QCD reformulated as constrained spin chains; integrable subsectors exist but full chain is non-integrable due to zigzag symmetry constraints; accurately predicts roughening transition; generalizes to higher dimensions.
AI.motivation: To study the strong coupling expansion of large N QCD by reformulating the Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian as constrained spin chain models and investigate their integrability properties.
AI.method: Reformulate Kogut-Susskind Hamiltonian on square lattice as constrained 1D spin chains; analyze integrability using Bethe ansatz approach; identify integrable subsectors; study effects of zigzag symmetry constraints; extrapolate first-order analytical results; generalize to higher dimensions.
AI.result: Large class of integrable subsectors exist, but full spin chain is non-integrable due to constraints from zigzag symmetry of confining strings; spin chain description accurately estimates roughening transition point; in higher dimensions, small subsectors without zigzag constraints remain integrable.
AI.conclusion: Large N QCD can be mapped to constrained spin chains with integrable subsectors, but full theory is non-integrable due to zigzag symmetry; this approach successfully predicts roughening transition and generalizes to higher dimensions.

title: Critical fluctuation patterns and anisotropic correlations driven by temperature gradients
summary: Studies of QCD phase transition signals are often conducted under spatially uniform temperature conditions. However, the influence of spatial temperature gradients on the signals emerging at the phase interface in the fireball generated by heavy-ion collisions has not yet been fully explored. Based on an Ising-like effective potential, we study the locally equilibrated systems with temperature gradients. In a 2D disk geometry, the low-energy fluctuation spectrum is explicitly resolved into radial and angular momentum modes. The nonlocal correaltions of singular eigen-mode exhibits strong anisotropy, which are long-ranged along isotherms but suppressed radially due to the thermal geometry of the system. Unlike homogeneous systems where the zero-momentum mode dominates, correlations in such inhomogeneous system result from the superposition of a series of zero and non-zero angular momentum modes with comparable contributions. We extract the singular angular momentum modes and establish their connection to experimentally observable anisotropic flow. We find azimuthally sensitive observables may offer a previously unexplored avenue for detecting the QCD phase transition.

AI.tldr: Study examines QCD phase transition signals in heavy-ion collisions with spatial temperature gradients, revealing anisotropic correlations along isotherms and suppressed radial correlations, connecting singular angular momentum modes to experimental anisotropic flow observables.
AI.motivation: Previous studies of QCD phase transition signals assume uniform temperature conditions, but real heavy-ion collisions create fireballs with spatial temperature gradients. The influence of these gradients on phase interface signals remains unexplored, motivating investigation of how temperature inhomogeneities affect correlation patterns.
AI.method: Using an Ising-like effective potential, researchers study locally equilibrated systems with temperature gradients in 2D disk geometry. They resolve low-energy fluctuation spectrum into radial and angular momentum modes, analyze nonlocal correlations of singular eigen-modes, and extract singular angular momentum modes to connect them to experimentally observable anisotropic flow.
AI.result: Correlations exhibit strong anisotropy: long-ranged along isotherms but suppressed radially due to thermal geometry. Unlike homogeneous systems where zero-momentum mode dominates, correlations in inhomogeneous systems result from superposition of zero and non-zero angular momentum modes with comparable contributions. Singular angular momentum modes are extracted and connected to anisotropic flow observables.
AI.conclusion: Azimuthally sensitive observables offer a previously unexplored avenue for detecting QCD phase transition in heavy-ion collisions. The anisotropic correlation patterns arising from temperature gradients provide distinctive signatures that differ from uniform temperature scenarios, potentially enabling new experimental detection methods.

title: Regge trajectories from the adjoint sector of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
summary: We reexamine the large $N$ limit of SU$(N)$ symmetric quantum mechanics of a Hermitian matrix whose singlet sector is well known to be exactly solvable via free fermions. When the Fermi level approaches a maximum of the potential, there is critical behavior corresponding to string theory in two dimensions. We uncover new phenomena in the adjoint sector by solving the Marchesini-Onofri equation both numerically and analytically using semiclassical approximations: at criticality, the spectrum is governed by Regge trajectories with energy eigenvalues growing according to $Δ^2 \sim n/ α'$. In the dual 2D string theory, we interpret these states as oscillatory excitations of a ``short'' folded open string. Up to sub-leading corrections, this Regge behavior is essentially universal and is insensitive to the particular potential we choose to approach criticality. Slightly away from criticality, the highly excited states transition into ``long strings'' that extend far into the Liouville direction.

AI.tldr: The paper reexamines SU(N) matrix quantum mechanics at large N, finding that near criticality (Fermi level at potential maximum), the adjoint sector exhibits Regge trajectories with Δ² ∼ n/α', interpreted as short folded open strings in dual 2D string theory.
AI.motivation: To extend understanding of SU(N) symmetric quantum mechanics beyond the well-known exactly solvable singlet sector, particularly examining the adjoint sector behavior near critical points where the Fermi level approaches a potential maximum, which corresponds to 2D string theory.
AI.method: Solve the Marchesini-Onofri equation both numerically and analytically using semiclassical approximations to study the spectrum in the adjoint sector near criticality.
AI.result: At criticality, the spectrum exhibits Regge trajectories with energy eigenvalues growing as Δ² ∼ n/α'. These states are interpreted as oscillatory excitations of short folded open strings in the dual 2D string theory. The behavior is universal up to sub-leading corrections and insensitive to the specific potential used to approach criticality. Slightly away from criticality, highly excited states transition into long strings extending into the Liouville direction.
AI.conclusion: The adjoint sector of SU(N) matrix quantum mechanics exhibits rich critical behavior with Regge trajectories that map to string excitations in the dual 2D string theory, revealing universal features of the critical point and connections between matrix models and string theory.

title: A smooth road to bumpy horizons: shaping black holes with non-linear sigma models, from supergravity to higher dimensions
summary: We construct new families of solutions for General Relativity coupled to a general class of non-linear sigma models, some of which can be embedded in supergravity. The solutions include neutral, charged and magnetized black holes with bumpy horizons, bumpy stars, and anisotropic cosmologies in $d\geq 4$ dimensions, as well as black strings and black $p$-branes. We also present a family of time-dependent solutions in $2+1$-dimensions. The construction relies on a set of first-order Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield relations for the coset scalars, that were recently exploited for the construction of bumpy black holes on the non-linear sigma model with homogenous target $SU(2)/U(1)$ in 2601.22914 [hep-th].

AI.motivation: To extend solution families in General Relativity coupled to non-linear sigma models (some embeddable in supergravity) beyond previous work on bumpy black holes, exploring various gravitational configurations.
AI.method: Construction relies on first-order Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) relations for coset scalars, extending techniques from previous work (2601.22914) on bumpy black holes in SU(2)/U(1) non-linear sigma model.

AI.conclusion: The BPS relations provide a powerful framework for constructing diverse gravitational solutions coupled to non-linear sigma models, significantly extending the known solution space beyond previously studied cases.

title: The Chern-Simons Natural Boundary and Black Hole Entropy
summary: The method of resurgent continuation of transseries reveals a new correspondence between the $q$-series for enumerating degeneracies of quarter-BPS states in supersymmetric black holes and $\hat{Z}$ invariants of Chern-Simons theory on a class of 3 dimensional orientation-reversed manifolds.

AI.tldr: Resurgent continuation of transseries establishes correspondence between q-series for quarter-BPS state degeneracies in supersymmetric black holes and $\hat{Z}$ invariants of Chern-Simons theory on 3D orientation-reversed manifolds.
AI.motivation: To uncover mathematical connections between seemingly distinct physical systems: supersymmetric black hole state counting (via q-series) and topological invariants in Chern-Simons theory, using advanced analytic continuation techniques.
AI.method: Resurgent continuation of transseries - an analytic continuation method that handles divergent series by considering their resurgence properties and Borel resummation, applied to compare q-series expansions from different physical contexts.

title: Muon collider experiments as electron/positron beam sources: case studies of new light-particle searches
summary: At muon colliders, muon decays naturally produce intense electrons and positrons with unique features, namely high energies, high repetition rates, and small intrinsic uncertainties, that are unavailable at existing accelerator facilities. We quantitatively study the feasibility of extracting such particles in two representative future muon collider designs, IMCC and $μ$TRISTAN. Using Monte Carlo simulations with the corresponding design parameters, we study the spatial, angular, and energy distributions of decay electrons and positrons in the curved sections of the collider ring. We find that typical deflections of $0.1-10~\mathrm{mrad}$ can be achieved even for high-energy electrons carrying large energy fractions ($\simeq 0.6 - 1.0$) of the muon beam energy, with the ring bending magnets (or magnets providing an equivalent field) effectively serving as a pre-septum magnet, that partially deflects the beam before the main septum magnet, suggesting that the extraction scheme could be practically feasible. Exploiting the distinct beam properties of IMCC and $μ$TRISTAN, we propose complementary search strategies, missing energy and momentum searches for dark matter at $μ$TRISTAN and visible-decay searches for axion-like particles and light scalars at IMCC, which probe parameter space beyond the reach of current and other proposed experiments.

AI.tldr: Muon colliders produce intense, high-energy electron/positron beams from muon decays that can be extracted for novel physics experiments, with two proposed designs (IMCC and μTRISTAN) enabling complementary dark matter and axion-like particle searches.
AI.motivation: Muon colliders naturally produce intense electron/positron beams with unique properties (high energy, high repetition rates, small uncertainties) that are unavailable at existing facilities. These beams could enable novel physics experiments beyond current capabilities.
AI.method: Used Monte Carlo simulations with design parameters of two future muon collider designs (IMCC and μTRISTAN) to study spatial, angular, and energy distributions of decay electrons/positrons in curved sections. Analyzed extraction feasibility using ring bending magnets as pre-septum magnets.
AI.result: Found that typical deflections of 0.1-10 mrad can be achieved even for high-energy electrons carrying large energy fractions (0.6-1.0) of muon beam energy. The bending magnets effectively serve as pre-septum magnets, making extraction practically feasible. Proposed complementary search strategies: missing energy/momentum searches for dark matter at μTRISTAN and visible-decay searches for axion-like particles and light scalars at IMCC.
AI.conclusion: Muon colliders offer a unique opportunity to extract intense, high-quality electron/positron beams for novel physics experiments. The proposed extraction scheme is feasible and enables complementary searches that probe parameter space beyond current and proposed experiments, particularly for dark matter and axion-like particles.

title: Holographic QCD and quarkonium melting: Finite temperature, density, and external field effects in self-consistent dynamical models
summary: This MSc dissertation is based on the papers arXiv:2502.12694 and arXiv:2408.14813. The AdS/CFT correspondence provides a powerful framework for modeling strongly coupled gauge theories and, as a consequence, investigating non-perturbative phenomena in QCD. In this work, following an overview of the ideas that encapsulate the AdS/CFT correspondence, we present a self-consistent dynamical holographic QCD model within the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton framework, derived from the coupled field equations, to study the mass spectra and melting behavior of heavy and exotic mesons at finite temperature and density. Finite temperature analyses reveal a confinement-deconfinement transition and sequential quarkonia melting. At finite density, an increase in chemical potential accelerates meson melting, with spectral functions evolving smoothly across the phase transition line. Finally, using a nonlinear Einstein-Born-Infeld-dilaton model, magnetic field effects demonstrate a shift from inverse magnetic catalysis to magnetic catalysis, highlighting the impact of spatial anisotropy on quarkonium stability.

AI.tldr: A holographic QCD model based on AdS/CFT correspondence studies heavy/exotic meson spectra and melting at finite temperature/density, revealing confinement-deconfinement transitions, sequential quarkonia melting, and magnetic field effects on meson stability.
AI.motivation: To investigate non-perturbative QCD phenomena using the AdS/CFT correspondence framework, specifically studying mass spectra and melting behavior of heavy and exotic mesons under finite temperature, density, and magnetic field conditions.
AI.method: Develops a self-consistent dynamical holographic QCD model within the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton framework derived from coupled field equations, with extensions to nonlinear Einstein-Born-Infeld-dilaton model for magnetic field effects.
AI.result: Finite temperature analysis reveals confinement-deconfinement transition and sequential quarkonia melting. Finite density increases chemical potential accelerates meson melting with smooth spectral function evolution across phase transition. Magnetic field effects show shift from inverse magnetic catalysis to magnetic catalysis, highlighting spatial anisotropy impact on quarkonium stability.
AI.conclusion: The holographic QCD model successfully captures key non-perturbative phenomena including confinement-deconfinement transitions, meson melting behavior under varying conditions, and magnetic field effects on quarkonium stability, demonstrating the power of AdS/CFT correspondence for studying strongly coupled gauge theories.

title: $N^{3/2}$ Scaling from $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ Dualities: an Alternative Approach to Chiral Quivers
summary: We investigate families of 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ chiral quiver gauge theories conjectured to be dual to M2-branes probing toric SE$_7$ singularities. Geometrically, these families correspond to toric diagrams without internal points. At the field theory level, the models are constructed via an un-higgsing procedure applied to non-chiral quivers. While the moduli space of these theories was shown to match M-theory expectations, determining the $N^{3/2}$ scaling of the free energy remained an open problem for over a decade, with positive results emerging only very recently. In this work, we address this challenge by reformulating the three-sphere partition function as a hyperbolic hypergeometric integral. Using exact integral identities, we show that the free energy reduces precisely to that of non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors, for which the $N^{3/2}$ scaling is already established. Physically, this mathematical identity corresponds to the equivalence of three-sphere partition functions under a generalization of Giveon-Kutasov duality to chiral quivers. Our results thus provide a large $N$ duality between the chiral quivers and non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors, confirming the $N^{3/2}$ scaling for the chiral quivers under study.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that 3D N=2 chiral quiver gauge theories dual to M2-branes probing toric SE7 singularities exhibit N^{3/2} scaling of free energy by showing their partition functions reduce to those of non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors through exact integral identities.
AI.motivation: For over a decade, determining the N^{3/2} scaling of free energy for 3D N=2 chiral quiver gauge theories dual to M2-branes probing toric SE7 singularities remained an open problem, despite evidence that their moduli spaces match M-theory expectations.
AI.method: Reformulate the three-sphere partition function as a hyperbolic hypergeometric integral, then use exact integral identities to show it reduces to the partition function of non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors, whose N^{3/2} scaling is already established.
AI.result: The free energy of chiral quivers reduces precisely to that of non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors, establishing N^{3/2} scaling for the chiral quivers. This corresponds to a generalization of Giveon-Kutasov duality to chiral quivers.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a large N duality between chiral quivers and non-chiral quivers with chiral flavors, confirming the N^{3/2} scaling for chiral quivers dual to M2-branes probing toric SE7 singularities.

title: TeV-scale unification of light dark matter and neutrino mass
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Comments are welcome
summary: We demonstrate that TeV-scale heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) responsible for inverse-seesaw neutrino mass generation can simultaneously fix the cosmological abundance and decay properties of dark matter (DM). The spontaneous breaking of lepton number gives rise to a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson that serves as a light DM candidate, whose mass originates from a small explicit breaking term. The same HNLs that generate neutrino masses produce the DM via freeze-in and mediate its decay into neutrinos, leading to a tight correlation among neutrino masses, DM relic abundance, and DM lifetime. For collider-accessible TeV-scale HNLs, the observed relic density and lifetime constraints point to sub-GeV DM, yielding observable neutrino signals at next-generation detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande, DUNE, and JUNO. This framework establishes a predictive and experimentally testable link between neutrino mass generation and dark matter.

AI.tldr: TeV-scale heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in inverse-seesaw models generate neutrino masses, produce sub-GeV dark matter via freeze-in, and mediate its decay to neutrinos, creating testable correlations between neutrino physics and dark matter properties.
AI.motivation: To establish a unified framework connecting neutrino mass generation (via inverse-seesaw mechanism) with dark matter properties, addressing both the origin of neutrino masses and the nature of dark matter simultaneously.
AI.method: Utilize TeV-scale heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in an inverse-seesaw model where spontaneous lepton number breaking produces a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson as dark matter candidate. The HNLs generate neutrino masses, produce DM via freeze-in production, and mediate DM decay into neutrinos.

AI.conclusion: The framework establishes a predictive and experimentally testable link between neutrino mass generation and dark matter, with specific predictions for observable neutrino signals at upcoming experiments.

title: Parameter compression in the flux landscape
summary: We present a data-driven investigation of the exhaustive ensemble of no-scale type IIB flux vacua constructed in \cite{Chauhan:2025rdj}. Using a combination of linear and non-linear dimensionality-reduction techniques, we analyse both flux and moduli spaces and demonstrate that the effective dimensionality of the underlying 12-dimensional flux space is substantially reduced. A central component of our study is a physics-informed autoencoder, which provides a non-linear compression of the flux and moduli data into a low-dimensional latent space. The learned latent representation organises vacua according to desired features and, in particular, isolates distinguished regions associated with small values of the flux superpotential $|W_0|$, revealing non-trivial correlations that are not captured by linear methods. In parallel, we apply tools from topological data analysis, specifically persistent homology, to probe the global structure of the vacuum distribution. This allows us to identify robust, long-lived topological features in both moduli and flux subspaces. This work is a necessary step for developing foundation models in string phenomenology.

AI.tldr: Data-driven analysis of no-scale type IIB flux vacua using dimensionality reduction, physics-informed autoencoders, and topological data analysis to reveal reduced effective dimensionality, correlations in flux space, and robust topological features.
AI.motivation: To systematically investigate the structure of no-scale type IIB flux vacua using modern data analysis techniques, moving beyond traditional analytic approaches to understand the effective dimensionality and organization of the vacuum landscape.
AI.method: Combination of linear and non-linear dimensionality reduction techniques, physics-informed autoencoder for non-linear compression of flux and moduli data into low-dimensional latent space, and persistent homology from topological data analysis to probe global structure.
AI.result: Effective dimensionality of the 12-dimensional flux space is substantially reduced; autoencoder reveals non-trivial correlations and isolates regions with small flux superpotential |W₀|; persistent homology identifies robust topological features in both moduli and flux subspaces.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates the power of modern data science techniques for analyzing string theory vacua, revealing hidden structure and correlations, and represents a necessary step toward developing foundation models in string phenomenology.

title: Effective vertexes in magnetized quark-gluon plasma
comment: 7 pages. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2408.01190
summary:
In quark-gluon plasma (QGP), at high temperatures $T$ the spontaneous generation of color magnetic fields, $b^3(T), b^8(T) \not = 0$ (3, 8 are color indexes), and usual magnetic field $b(T) \not = 0$ happens. Also, the Polyakov loop and related to it the $A_0(T)$ condensate, which is solution to Yang-Mills imaginary time equations, create.
  Recently, with the new type two-loop effective potential, which generalizes the known integral representation for the Bernoulli polynomials and takes into consideration the magnetic background, these effects were derived.
  The corresponding effective potential $W(T, b^3, b^8, b, A_0 )$ was calculated either in SU(2) gluodynamics or full quantum chromodynamics (QCD). The values of magnetic field strengths at different temperatures were calculated and the mechanism for stabilizing the background due to $A_0(T)$ was also discovered.
  In present paper, we concentrate on the one-loop quark contributions. In particular, we derive the effective vertexes, which couple magnetic fields and $A_0$. The vertexes result in new specific effects signalling the creation of QGP in heavy ion collision experiments.
  Key words: spontaneous magnetization, high temperature, asymptotic freedom, effective potential, $A_0$ condensate, effective vertexes.

AI.tldr: The paper studies spontaneous generation of color magnetic fields and A₀ condensate in quark-gluon plasma at high temperatures, focusing on one-loop quark contributions and deriving effective vertices coupling magnetic fields with A₀ that signal QGP creation in heavy ion collisions.
AI.motivation: To understand the spontaneous generation of color magnetic fields (b³, b⁸) and usual magnetic fields (b) in quark-gluon plasma at high temperatures, along with the Polyakov loop and A₀ condensate, and to investigate how one-loop quark contributions create effective vertices that couple these fields and signal QGP formation in heavy ion collisions.
AI.method: Uses a new type of two-loop effective potential that generalizes the integral representation for Bernoulli polynomials and incorporates magnetic background. Calculates effective potential W(T, b³, b⁸, b, A₀) in both SU(2) gluodynamics and full QCD, then focuses on one-loop quark contributions to derive effective vertices coupling magnetic fields with A₀.
AI.result: Calculated magnetic field strengths at different temperatures, discovered the mechanism for stabilizing the background due to A₀(T), and derived effective vertices that couple magnetic fields with A₀, resulting in new specific effects that signal QGP creation in heavy ion collision experiments.
AI.conclusion: One-loop quark contributions generate effective vertices that couple magnetic fields with the A₀ condensate, producing observable signatures of quark-gluon plasma formation in heavy ion collisions, with implications for understanding spontaneous magnetization and background stabilization mechanisms in high-temperature QCD.

title: Gravitational instantons from closed superstring field theory
comment: 21 pages; partially based on the master's thesis of one of the authors
summary: We test exact marginality of the deformation describing the resolution of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold by analyzing the closed superstring equations of motion to third order in the size, including $α'$ corrections. We find that the third order correction is unobstructed for all deformation moduli. We are also able to reproduce the Eguchi-Hanson gravitational instanton up to the second order in the field theory limit with a suitable choice of moduli.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes exact marginality of deformations resolving a Z2 orbifold by examining closed superstring equations of motion to third order in size, including α' corrections, finding unobstructed third-order corrections for all deformation moduli and reproducing the Eguchi-Hanson gravitational instanton in field theory limit.
AI.motivation: To test whether deformations describing the resolution of a Z2 orbifold are exactly marginal in string theory, going beyond leading order approximations to include higher-order α' corrections and verify consistency with known gravitational instanton solutions.
AI.method: Analyze closed superstring equations of motion to third order in the deformation size parameter, including α' corrections, and examine the field theory limit by comparing with the Eguchi-Hanson gravitational instanton solution.
AI.result: The third-order correction is unobstructed for all deformation moduli, indicating exact marginality persists beyond leading order. The Eguchi-Hanson gravitational instanton is reproduced up to second order in the field theory limit with appropriate moduli choices.
AI.conclusion: The deformation describing Z2 orbifold resolution remains exactly marginal to third order in string theory, with consistency established between the string theory analysis and known gravitational instanton solutions in the field theory limit.

title: Axial-vector neutral-current measurements in coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments
summary: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) is predominantly governed by vector neutral-current interactions, with subleading contributions arising from the axial current in nuclei with non-zero ground-state spin. Experimentally, the extraction of axial-current contributions has been so far of little interest, mainly because of the challenges its measurement entail. In this work, we investigate the relative size of the vector and axial components for target materials currently employed by the neutrino and dark matter experimental communities. We identify fluorine-based compounds as the most promising targets for probing the axial-current event rate. Among them, octafluoropropane ($\text{C}_3\text{F}_8$) emerges as a particularly suitable candidate, given its widespread use in spin-dependent dark matter searches and its relevance for upcoming dedicated CE$ν$NS experiments. Considering both pion decay-at-rest and reactor neutrino fluxes, we show that such measurements can allow an indirect determination of the axial coupling at the $\sim 10\%$ level, depending on flux uncertainties and detector thresholds. We further emphasize that measurements of the axial current will allow to probe spin-dependent new physics scenarios through CE$ν$NS.

AI.tldr: Analysis of axial-current contributions in coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, identifying fluorine-based compounds (especially C₃F₈) as optimal targets for probing axial coupling at ~10% precision using reactor or pion decay-at-rest neutrino sources.
AI.motivation: CEνNS experiments have focused on vector neutral-current interactions, neglecting axial-current contributions due to measurement challenges. However, axial components become significant for nuclei with non-zero ground-state spin, offering opportunities to probe spin-dependent new physics and determine axial couplings.
AI.method: Systematic investigation of relative vector/axial component sizes for target materials used in neutrino and dark matter experiments. Identification of fluorine-based compounds as optimal targets, with octafluoropropane (C₃F₈) highlighted due to its use in spin-dependent dark matter searches and relevance for upcoming CEνNS experiments. Analysis using both pion decay-at-rest and reactor neutrino fluxes.
AI.result: Fluorine-based compounds identified as most promising for axial-current measurements. C₃F₈ emerges as particularly suitable candidate. Measurements can achieve ~10% precision in axial coupling determination, depending on flux uncertainties and detector thresholds. Demonstrates feasibility of probing spin-dependent new physics through CEνNS.
AI.conclusion: Axial-current contributions in CEνNS, previously neglected, offer valuable physics opportunities. Fluorine targets like C₃F₈ enable precision measurements of axial couplings and access to spin-dependent new physics scenarios, expanding the physics reach of CEνNS experiments beyond vector interactions.

title: Simulating Lattice Gauge Theories with Virtual Rishons
summary: Classical tensor network and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms are promising candidates for the investigation of real-time properties of lattice gauge theories. We develop here a novel framework which enforces gauge symmetry via a quantum-link virtual rishon representation applied at intermediate steps. Crucially, the gauge and matter degrees of freedom are dynamical variables encoded in terms of qubits, enabling analysis of gauge theories in $d+1$ spacetime dimensions. We benchmark this framework in a U(1) gauge theory with and without matter fields. For $d = 1$, the multi-flavor Schwinger model with $1\leq N_f\leq3$ flavors is analyzed for arbitrary boundary conditions and nonzero topological angle, capturing signatures of the underlying Wess-Zumino-Witten conformal field theory. For $d = 2$, we extract the confining string tension in close agreement with continuum expectations. These results establish the virtual rishon framework as a scalable and robust approach for the simulation of lattice gauge theories using both classical tensor networks as well as near-term quantum hardware.

AI.tldr: A novel virtual rishon framework for simulating lattice gauge theories using tensor networks and quantum hardware, benchmarked on U(1) gauge theories in 1D and 2D.
AI.motivation: To develop a scalable framework for investigating real-time properties of lattice gauge theories that enforces gauge symmetry and works with both classical tensor networks and near-term quantum hardware.
AI.method: A quantum-link virtual rishon representation that enforces gauge symmetry at intermediate steps, encoding gauge and matter degrees of freedom as qubits for analysis in d+1 spacetime dimensions.
AI.result: Successfully benchmarked on U(1) gauge theory: for d=1, analyzed multi-flavor Schwinger model with 1≤N_f≤3 flavors, arbitrary boundary conditions, nonzero topological angle, capturing Wess-Zumino-Witten CFT signatures; for d=2, extracted confining string tension in close agreement with continuum expectations.
AI.conclusion: The virtual rishon framework establishes a scalable and robust approach for simulating lattice gauge theories using both classical tensor networks and near-term quantum hardware.

title: The eV-Scale Sterile Neutrino and Neutrinoless Double Beta Decay
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, Published in Physics of Particles and Nuclei Letters
summary: In short-baseline experiments such as LSND and MiniBooNE, an excess of electron neutrinos has been observed, originating from a muon neutrino beam. To address this anomaly, in the line of many works, we investigate various neutrino mixing schemes involving eV-scale sterile neutrinos alongside three active neutrinos. Using updated experimental and global fit data, we studied neutrinoless double beta decay for three different schemes such as 3+1, 1 + 3, and 2 + 2, which involve one sterile neutrino and three active neutrinos. We have done analysis of these schemes for normal hierarchy (NH) as well as for inverted hierarchy (IH) frameworks, and constrained the sterile neutrino mass in light of current and future neutrinoless double beta decay experiments. The 3+1 scheme is found to be the most viable and at the level of $3σ$ the mass of sterile neutrino with respect to the lightest neutrino mass ($m_{\text{lightest}}$) is restricted to $4.75~eV$ for the NH and $4.72~eV$ for the IH. Additionally, the limits on the sum of four neutrino masses are determined to be $4.81~eV$ for the normal hierarchy and $4.78~eV$ for the inverted hierarchy. The updated analysis of all these schemes would help us in understanding physics governing neutrinoless double beta decay and limit on the mass of sterile neutrinos.

AI.tldr: Analysis of neutrino mixing schemes with eV-scale sterile neutrinos to explain LSND/MiniBooNE anomalies, focusing on neutrinoless double beta decay constraints for 3+1, 1+3, and 2+2 models under both normal and inverted hierarchies.
AI.motivation: To address the electron neutrino excess observed in short-baseline experiments (LSND and MiniBooNE) by investigating sterile neutrino mixing schemes and constraining sterile neutrino masses using neutrinoless double beta decay data.
AI.method: Analysis of three neutrino mixing schemes (3+1, 1+3, 2+2) involving one sterile neutrino and three active neutrinos, using updated experimental and global fit data. Studied both normal hierarchy (NH) and inverted hierarchy (IH) frameworks, constraining sterile neutrino mass in light of current and future neutrinoless double beta decay experiments.
AI.result: The 3+1 scheme is most viable, with sterile neutrino mass limited to 4.75 eV for NH and 4.72 eV for IH at 3σ confidence level. Sum of four neutrino masses constrained to 4.81 eV (NH) and 4.78 eV (IH).
AI.conclusion: Updated analysis of sterile neutrino mixing schemes provides constraints on sterile neutrino masses through neutrinoless double beta decay, helping understand the physics governing this process and limiting sterile neutrino parameters.

title: Introduction to holography
summary: These are course notes for the 'Introduction to holography' Master level course at University of Cologne. The goal of the course is to give a pedogogical introduction to holography. Holography is a popular approach to quantum gravity, in which a theory of gravity can be described by a lower-dimensional boundary theory that itself has no gravity. The most concrete known example of a holographic model is the AdS/CFT correspondence, where the gravitational theory has a negative cosmological constant (the universe is asymptotically Anti-de Sitter) and the boundary theory is a conformal field theory. Symmetry plays a very important role in this duality. We therefore start the course with a review of Poincaré symmetry in quantum field theory, before moving on in the second chapter to conformal symmetry in conformally invariant quantum field theories or CFT's. Then we move to the basics of AdS physics in chapters 3 and 4, which will already reveal hints to the existence of a duality with CFT. After gathering the basic ingredients (CFT and AdS), in the second half of the course we are ready to formulate the AdS/CFT correspondence (chapter 5), including finite temperature AdS/CFT (chapter 6), which involves black holes and their thermodynamics in the gravitational theory (chapter 7). We end the course with an introduction to entanglement in AdS/CFT and the origin of statements that 'gravity emerges from entanglement' in holography.

AI.tldr: Course notes providing pedagogical introduction to holography, focusing on AdS/CFT correspondence as concrete example where gravitational theory in Anti-de Sitter space is dual to conformal field theory on boundary.
AI.motivation: To provide accessible pedagogical introduction to holography for Master's students, explaining how gravity can emerge from non-gravitational boundary theories, with AdS/CFT as primary example.
AI.method: Structured course approach: starts with Poincaré symmetry in QFT, progresses to conformal symmetry in CFTs, then introduces AdS physics, formulates AdS/CFT correspondence, covers finite temperature aspects with black holes, and concludes with entanglement in holography.
AI.result: Comprehensive course notes covering fundamental concepts: symmetry foundations, AdS geometry, CFT basics, AdS/CFT dictionary, black hole thermodynamics in holography, and entanglement's role in emergent gravity.
AI.conclusion: Holography provides powerful framework where gravitational physics emerges from non-gravitational boundary theories, with AdS/CFT correspondence offering concrete realization and entanglement playing crucial role in emergence of spacetime geometry.

title: Exploring $T_{ΥΥ}$ tetraquark candidates in a coupled-channels formalism
summary: We investigate the spectrum of $T_{ΥΥ}$ tetraquark candidates within a coupled-channels framework. The analysis includes all $L\leq2$ combinations of $Υ(1S)$, $Υ(2S)$, $η_b(1S)$, and $η_b(2S)$ in the $J^P = 0^\pm, 1^\pm, 2^\pm$ sectors. The meson-meson interaction is derived from an underlying constituent quark model through the resonating group method, and the properties of the states are obtained from poles of the scattering matrix. We find a rich spectrum of resonant, and virtual, states distributed between the $η_b(1S)η_b(1S)$ and $Υ(2S)Υ(2S)$ thresholds. The pattern of poles exhibits approximate heavy-quark spin symmetry multiplets. Several states are dominated by a single channel and can be associated with threshold-driven structures, while higher-mass resonances show sizable mixing among channels involving radially excited bottomonia. The predicted widths range from tens to several hundred MeV. Branching ratios indicate that many states couple predominantly to final states with at least one excited bottomonium, whereas only a subset of the spectrum is expected to be visible in the $η_b(1S)η_b(1S)$, $η_b(1S)Υ(1S)$ and $Υ(1S)Υ(1S)$ channels. These results provide quantitative guidance for experimental searches of fully heavy tetraquarks and offer a test of coupled-channel dynamics and heavy-quark spin symmetry in the $bb\bar b\bar b$ sector.

AI.method: Coupled-channels framework including all $L\leq2$ combinations of $Υ(1S)$, $Υ(2S)$, $η_b(1S)$, and $η_b(2S)$ in $J^P = 0^\pm, 1^\pm, 2^\pm$ sectors. Meson-meson interaction derived from underlying constituent quark model through resonating group method. State properties obtained from poles of scattering matrix.
AI.result: Rich spectrum of resonant and virtual states distributed between $η_b(1S)η_b(1S)$ and $Υ(2S)Υ(2S)$ thresholds. Pattern shows approximate heavy-quark spin symmetry multiplets. Some states dominated by single channels (threshold-driven structures), while higher-mass resonances show sizable mixing among channels with radially excited bottomonia. Widths range from tens to several hundred MeV. Many states couple predominantly to final states with at least one excited bottomonium.

title: Discrete \texorpdfstring{$θ$}{theta} Projection: A Gauge-Protected Solution to the Strong CP Problem Without Axions
summary: We address the strong CP problem: why the physical QCD angle theta-bar must be extraordinarily small given the stringent bounds on the neutron electric dipole moment. Peccei-Quinn axion models can relax theta-bar dynamically, but rely on an approximate global symmetry expected to be violated by quantum gravity and face severe astrophysical and cosmological constraints. We propose Discrete theta Projection, an axionless, gauge-protected resolution obtained by gauging a finite cyclic subgroup $Z_N $of the $2π$ shift symmetry of theta. Coupling QCD to a compact, local and gapped topological sector orbifolds the path integral, identifying theta values that differ by $2π/N$ and admitting only instanton sectors whose topological charge lies in $Z_N$. In the large four-volume limit the vacuum energy becomes the lower envelope of the orbifold images, so the theory dynamically selects the branch closest to the CP-symmetric point, enforcing $|\barθ| \le π/N$ without assuming any prior smallness. Because the discrete shift is gauged, continuous renormalization of theta is forbidden; the construction can be formulated via higher-form/two-group structure with integer-quantized couplings fixed by anomaly inflow, ensuring radiative and gravitational stability and satisfying mixed gauge-gravity consistency conditions. The framework predicts a neutron EDM suppressed by $1/N$, no axion signatures, no domain-wall/isocurvature issues, and lattice diagnostics: piecewise-analytic theta dependence with cusps at odd fractions of the reduced period and a global curvature scaling as $1/N^2$. We provide the EFT construction, a nonperturbative proof of vacuum projection, a full anomaly analysis, and UV embeddings (including discrete clockwork chains) that generate large effective N while preserving integrality and consistency throughout.

AI.tldr: Discrete theta Projection solves the strong CP problem by gauging a finite cyclic subgroup of theta's shift symmetry, dynamically enforcing |θ̄| ≤ π/N without axions or fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: The strong CP problem requires θ̄ to be extremely small (<10^{-10}) to match neutron EDM bounds. Axion solutions face issues: they rely on approximate global symmetries (violated by quantum gravity) and have astrophysical/cosmological constraints. A gauge-protected, axionless solution is needed.
AI.method: Gauge a finite cyclic subgroup Z_N of the 2π shift symmetry of θ. Couple QCD to a compact topological sector that orbifolds the path integral, identifying θ values differing by 2π/N. Only instanton sectors with topological charge in Z_N are allowed. The construction uses higher-form/two-group structure with integer-quantized couplings fixed by anomaly inflow.
