Continuous θ renormalization forbidden. Predicts neutron EDM suppressed by 1/N, no axion signatures, no domain-wall/isocurvature issues, piecewise-analytic θ dependence with cusps, curvature scaling as 1/N^2.
AI.conclusion: Discrete theta Projection provides a gauge-protected, axionless solution to strong CP problem that is radiatively and gravitationally stable, satisfies consistency conditions, and can be embedded in UV completions (like discrete clockwork chains) with large effective N while preserving integrality.

title: Renormalization and Factorization Scale-Invariant Predictions for the Higgs Rare Decay $H\to J/ψ+γ$ via the Principle of Maximum Conformality
summary: We investigate the \(J/ψ\) direct production mechanism in the rare exclusive Higgs decay \(H\to J/ψ+γ\) within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD), which provides a clean probe for extracting the charm-quark Yukawa coupling to the Higgs boson. The Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) is used to remove conventional renormalization-scheme and scale ambiguities in the next-to-next-to-leading-order (N\(^2\)LO) perturbative QCD series. Large logarithmic contributions arising from Yukawa coupling renormalization are resummed, providing a reliable foundation for subsequent analyses. Using the experimentally measured leptonic decay width of \(J/ψ\) and the N\(^2\)LO perturbative result, we extract the factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix element \(\langle J/ψ({\bm ε})|ψ^{\dagger}{\bm σ}\cdot{\bm ε}χ(μ_Λ) |0\rangle\). Combining this with the factorization-scale-dependent short-distance coefficient, we obtain a factorization-scale-invariant decay width for the channel. Compared with earlier predictions in the literature, our fixed-order result for \(Γ(H\to J/ψ+γ)\) is more robust and precise, with good convergence and no renormalization- or factorization-scale dependence. We find \(Γ(H\to J/ψ+γ) = (6.4574^{+0.3995}_{-0.3995}) \times 10^{-11}\) GeV, where the uncertainty is the quadratic sum of contributions from \(Δα_s(m_Z) = \pm 0.0009\), \(ΔΓ_{J/ψ\to e^+e^-} = \pm 0.10\ \text{GeV}\), \(Δ\overline{m}_c(\overline{m}_c) = \pm 0.0046\ \text{GeV}\), and the estimated magnitude of N\(^3\)LO contributions from Bayesian analysis. This work demonstrates for the first time how the PMC can be applied to obtain fixed-order perturbative predictions that are invariant under both renormalization and factorization scale variations.

AI.tldr: PMC-based N²LO NRQCD analysis of H→J/ψ+γ decay provides precise, scale-invariant prediction for extracting charm-quark Yukawa coupling.
AI.motivation: To provide a clean probe for extracting the charm-quark Yukawa coupling to the Higgs boson through the rare exclusive decay H→J/ψ+γ, addressing renormalization-scheme and scale ambiguities in perturbative QCD calculations.
AI.method: Uses nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework with Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) to remove renormalization-scheme and scale ambiguities at N²LO. Large logarithmic contributions from Yukawa coupling renormalization are resummed. Combines experimentally measured J/ψ leptonic decay width with N²LO perturbative result to extract factorization-scale-dependent long-distance matrix element, then combines with short-distance coefficient to obtain factorization-scale-invariant decay width.
AI.result: Obtained Γ(H→J/ψ+γ) = (6.4574^{+0.3995}_{-0.3995}) × 10^{-11} GeV with uncertainties from α_s, Γ_{J/ψ→e⁺e⁻}, charm quark mass, and estimated N³LO contributions. Result shows good convergence and no renormalization- or factorization-scale dependence, providing more robust and precise prediction than earlier literature.
AI.conclusion: First demonstration of PMC application to obtain fixed-order perturbative predictions invariant under both renormalization and factorization scale variations. Provides reliable foundation for extracting charm-quark Yukawa coupling from H→J/ψ+γ decay with significantly reduced theoretical uncertainties.

title: 3d-3d correspondence and abelian flat connection
summary: We realize a homological block of a knot complement in $S^3$ for $G_{\mathbb{C}}=SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ as a half-index of a 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory via an expression of the homological block as an inverted Habiro series by working out some examples, which we expect to extend to general knots. Also, by choosing a certain set of poles in the integral expression of the half-index, we obtain the colored Jones polynomial.

AI.tldr: Homological blocks of knot complements in S³ for G_C=SL(2,C) are realized as half-indices of 3d N=2 theories via inverted Habiro series, with colored Jones polynomials obtained from specific pole choices.
AI.motivation: To establish a connection between homological invariants of knot complements and 3d supersymmetric quantum field theories, specifically realizing homological blocks as physical observables (half-indices) in 3d N=2 theories.
AI.method: Express homological blocks as inverted Habiro series, then realize them as half-indices of 3d N=2 theories. Use integral expressions of half-indices and select specific pole configurations to obtain colored Jones polynomials.
AI.result: Successfully realized homological blocks for SL(2,C) knot complements as half-indices via inverted Habiro series for example knots, with expectation of generalization to all knots. Demonstrated that colored Jones polynomials emerge from specific pole choices in the half-index integral.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a concrete connection between knot homological invariants and 3d supersymmetric field theories, providing a physical interpretation of homological blocks as half-indices and showing how colored Jones polynomials naturally arise from this framework.

title: Evaluation of Feynman integrals via numerical integration of differential equations
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, talk given at RADCOR2025
summary: We revisit the idea of numerically integrating the differential form of Feynman integrals. With a novel approach for the treatment of branch cuts, we develop an integrator capable of evaluating a basis of master integrals in double and quadruple precision, with significantly smaller run times than other tools. This opens the door to evaluating higher complexity Feynman integrals on the fly in Monte Carlo generators, and enables a cheaper and easy to parallelise generation of grids for the topologies with prohibitive computational times. To show its performance, we test one- and two-loop integral families, achieving evaluation times in double precision of milliseconds and hundreds of milliseconds, respectively. We comment on the results and suggest room for improvement.

AI.tldr: Novel numerical integration method for Feynman integrals with improved branch cut treatment, achieving millisecond-scale evaluation times for one- and two-loop integrals.
AI.motivation: Enable faster evaluation of Feynman integrals for Monte Carlo generators and reduce computational costs for complex topologies that currently have prohibitive run times.
AI.method: Numerical integration of differential form of Feynman integrals with novel approach for handling branch cuts, implemented in double and quadruple precision integrator.
AI.result: Achieved evaluation times of milliseconds for one-loop integrals and hundreds of milliseconds for two-loop integrals in double precision, significantly faster than existing tools.
AI.conclusion: The method enables on-the-fly evaluation of higher complexity Feynman integrals in Monte Carlo generators and provides cheaper, easily parallelizable grid generation for computationally intensive topologies.

title: Constraints on millicharged particles from thunderstorms on the Solar system planets
summary: We investigate the production of millicharged particles (mCPs) by the Schwinger mechanism in thunderstorms in the atmospheres of different planets in the Solar system. We study both fermion and scalar mCPs; for scalar mCPs, we take into account the effect of Bose enhancement. We use the observational data of planetary atmospheres obtained by satellite missions to establish constraints on the charge and mass of mCP particles. The best constraints came from the observation of thunderstorms in Saturn's atmosphere: $q > 10^{-11}$ for fermionic mCP and $q > 10^{-24}$ for bosonic mCPs. These constraints are, to the best of our knowledge, the best in the literature.

AI.tldr: Study of millicharged particle production via Schwinger mechanism in planetary thunderstorms, establishing constraints on mCP charge and mass using satellite atmospheric data.
AI.motivation: To investigate the production of millicharged particles through the Schwinger mechanism in thunderstorm environments across different Solar System planets, leveraging planetary atmospheric data to constrain mCP properties.
AI.method: Analyze mCP production via Schwinger mechanism in thunderstorm electric fields across planetary atmospheres; study both fermionic and scalar mCPs with Bose enhancement for scalars; use observational satellite data of planetary atmospheres to establish constraints.
AI.result: Best constraints from Saturn's thunderstorms: q > 10^{-11} for fermionic mCPs and q > 10^{-24} for bosonic mCPs, representing the strongest constraints in the literature.
AI.conclusion: Planetary thunderstorms provide powerful environments for constraining millicharged particle properties via Schwinger mechanism, with Saturn's atmosphere yielding the most stringent limits to date.

title: On curvature corrections for field theory cosmic strings
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures. Comments are welcome. A movie of the simulation can be found in https://youtu.be/0qi1brTlTSg
summary: We present a combined analytical and numerical study of the effective action of field theory cosmic strings in the Abelian-Higgs model in flat space. Starting directly from the underlying solitonic field theory description, we provide a systematic derivation of the low energy effective action and present evidence for the absence of nontrivial curvature correction terms when only the translational Goldstone modes are retained. Using this framework, we extend the effective theory to include higher energy fluctuations of the soliton profile, which map to massive degrees of freedom propagating on the worldsheet. We show that the leading curvature contribution enters only through the coupling between these massive modes and the worldsheet Ricci scalar. We validate the resulting effective theory via lattice simulations of the full field theory equations of motion in flat space, implemented with Adaptive Mesh Refinement to capture the string dynamics across different scales. The numerical simulations confirm the dynamics obtained using the effective action in its validity range. Furthermore, they also demonstrate the existence of the predicted parametric instability of excited strings that drives the transfer of energy from massive excitations to the Goldstone sector.

AI.tldr: Study of effective action for cosmic strings in Abelian-Higgs model shows no curvature corrections for translational modes alone, but curvature enters through coupling between massive modes and worldsheet Ricci scalar, validated by AMR lattice simulations.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive the low-energy effective action for cosmic strings from the underlying solitonic field theory description, understand the role of curvature corrections, and extend the effective theory to include massive degrees of freedom beyond just Goldstone modes.
AI.method: Combined analytical and numerical approach: 1) Systematic derivation of effective action from Abelian-Higgs model field theory, 2) Extension to include massive fluctuations of soliton profile, 3) Validation via lattice simulations of full field theory equations using Adaptive Mesh Refinement to capture multi-scale string dynamics.
AI.result: 1) No nontrivial curvature correction terms when only translational Goldstone modes are retained, 2) Leading curvature contribution enters through coupling between massive modes and worldsheet Ricci scalar, 3) Numerical simulations confirm effective action dynamics in validity range, 4) Demonstration of predicted parametric instability driving energy transfer from massive excitations to Goldstone sector.
AI.conclusion: The effective action for cosmic strings has a specific structure where curvature effects only appear through interactions with massive modes, not through pure Goldstone dynamics, and this framework is validated by numerical simulations that also reveal energy transfer mechanisms between different excitation sectors.

title: Lepton mixing and charged lepton flavour violation from inverse seesaw with non-degenerate heavy states
summary: We analyse an inverse seesaw scenario with 3+3 gauge singlets. The flavour structure is determined by a flavour symmetry, Delta (3 n^2) or Delta (6 n^2), n integer, and CP and their residual groups among charged leptons and the neutral states. For the latter, the Dirac mass matrix of the gauge singlets carries all non-trivial flavour structure. Consequently, the heavy sterile states form three pseudo-Dirac pairs which have in general distinct masses. We discuss the signal strength of different charged lepton flavour violating processes. Ensuring that the lepton mixing angles can be accommodated at the 3 sigma level or better, we find that the current bounds on the branching ratios of mu -> e gamma, mu -> 3 e, tau -> l gamma and tau -> 3 l, l=e, mu, as well as the rate of mu-e conversion in nuclei do not strongly constrain the considered parameter space, while the limits expected from the upcoming experiments Mu3E, COMET and Mu2e will have a relevant impact.

AI.tldr: Inverse seesaw model with 3+3 gauge singlets using Delta(3n²) or Delta(6n²) flavor symmetry and CP symmetry predicts three pseudo-Dirac sterile neutrino pairs with distinct masses; current charged lepton flavor violation bounds are weak but upcoming experiments will strongly constrain parameter space.
AI.motivation: To construct a predictive flavor model for neutrino masses and mixing using discrete flavor symmetries (Delta(3n²) or Delta(6n²)) combined with CP symmetry, while analyzing the phenomenological consequences for charged lepton flavor violation processes in an inverse seesaw framework.
AI.method: Analyze an inverse seesaw scenario with 3+3 gauge singlets where flavor structure is determined by Delta(3n²) or Delta(6n²) flavor symmetry and CP symmetry. The Dirac mass matrix of gauge singlets carries all non-trivial flavor structure, leading to three pseudo-Dirac pairs of heavy sterile states with generally distinct masses. Study signal strengths of various charged lepton flavor violating processes.
AI.result: Current bounds on branching ratios of μ→eγ, μ→3e, τ→ℓγ and τ→3ℓ (ℓ=e,μ), as well as μ-e conversion in nuclei do not strongly constrain the considered parameter space when lepton mixing angles are accommodated at 3σ level or better. However, upcoming experiments (Mu3E, COMET, Mu2e) will have relevant impact on constraining the parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The inverse seesaw model with discrete flavor symmetries and CP symmetry provides a predictive framework compatible with current neutrino oscillation data and charged lepton flavor violation bounds, but will be significantly tested by next-generation experiments searching for lepton flavor violation.

title: Gauge-string duality, monomial bases and graph determinants
summary: Questions at the intersection of the AdS/CFT correspondence and quantum information theory motivate the study of projectors in sequences of subalgebras of finite-dimensional commutative associative semisimple algebras $\mathcal{A}$, obtained by incrementally adjoining one generator at each step to produce a non-linear generating set for $\mathcal{A}$. We define degeneracy graphs, which are finite layered tree graphs whose nodes represent projectors in the successive subalgebras. Using combinatorial properties of the degeneracy graph, we give a simple formula for constructing a linear basis of $\mathcal{A}$ in terms of monomials in the generators.The nodes can be labelled by formal variables corresponding to the eigenvalues of the generators added at each layer. We prove that the construction is compatible with the required counting of projectors in $\mathcal{A}$, and give explicit constructions of the projectors in terms of the monomials, in the cases of one- and two-layer degeneracy graphs with arbitrary numbers of nodes. More generally, we provide extensive computational evidence for the invertibility of the matrix relating the proposed monomial basis to the projector basis, by evaluating its determinant. In the 1-layer case, this is a Vandermonde determinant. A simple formula for the non-vanishing determinant in the general layer case is conjectured and supported by the computational data. The construction is illustrated with examples including centres of symmetric group algebras and maximally commuting subalgebras generated by JucysMurphy elements. We outline applications of the monomial basis to algorithms for constructing matrix units in non-commutative semisimple algebras, with relevance to orthogonal bases of multi-matrix gauge-invariant operators and to quantum information theory.

AI.tldr: The paper studies projectors in sequences of subalgebras of finite-dimensional commutative semisimple algebras, introduces degeneracy graphs to represent these projectors, and constructs a monomial basis for the algebra with applications to matrix units and quantum information theory.
AI.motivation: Motivated by questions at the intersection of AdS/CFT correspondence and quantum information theory, the paper aims to understand projectors in sequences of commutative subalgebras and construct explicit bases for these algebras.
AI.method: Defines degeneracy graphs (finite layered tree graphs) whose nodes represent projectors in successive subalgebras. Uses combinatorial properties to derive a formula for constructing a linear basis in terms of monomials in generators. Proves compatibility with projector counting and provides explicit constructions for one- and two-layer cases.
AI.result: Provides a simple formula for constructing monomial basis, proves compatibility with projector counting, gives explicit projector constructions for one- and two-layer cases, and provides computational evidence for invertibility of the monomial-to-projector matrix. Conjectures a determinant formula for general cases.
AI.conclusion: The degeneracy graph approach successfully constructs monomial bases for commutative semisimple algebras, with applications to constructing matrix units in non-commutative algebras, orthogonal bases of gauge-invariant operators, and quantum information theory.

title: Connecting Flavor and Baryon Asymmetry via Leptogenesis in Effective Froggatt-Nielsen Theory
summary: We investigate the hierarchical flavor structure of the Standard Model in a Froggatt-Nielsen (FN) framework, where the spontaneous breaking of a $U(1)_{\rm FN}$ symmetry by a complex flavon field generates fermion masses and mixing patterns through higher-dimensional operators. Extending the setup with three right-handed neutrinos (RHNs), light neutrino masses arise via the Type-I seesaw mechanism. Allowing complex FN coefficients enables a consistent description of the CKM and PMNS matrices while inducing CP-violating signatures in meson decays. Building on our previous work, where the lightest RHN acts as a viable dark matter (DM) candidate produced through freeze-in or freeze-out mechanisms, we investigate the origin of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe. The heavier RHNs generate a lepton asymmetry through out-of-equilibrium decays, including both Standard Model channels and additional flavon-induced processes in which the flavon appears as an intermediate or final-state particle. We compute the corresponding one-loop CP asymmetries and incorporate these effects in the Boltzmann equations. We show that although freeze-in and freeze-out DM production occur in two qualitatively distinct regions of the FN symmetry-breaking scale $v_φ$, successful thermal leptogenesis can be achieved in both regimes. In the large-$v_φ$ (freeze-in-compatible) region the results approach the standard leptogenesis limit, while in the freeze-out-compatible region the lower value of $v_φ$ implies lighter RHNs, requiring resonant enhancement. This tightly constrained framework, in which $v_φ$ simultaneously controls RHN masses and the interaction strengths of the flavon and DM sectors, provides a predictive and unified description of flavor hierarchies, neutrino masses, CP violation, dark matter, and baryogenesis within a single effective theory.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a unified Froggatt-Nielsen framework that simultaneously explains flavor hierarchies, neutrino masses, CP violation, dark matter, and baryogenesis through a single U(1) symmetry breaking mechanism.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive explanation of multiple fundamental phenomena—flavor structure, neutrino masses, CP violation, dark matter, and baryon asymmetry—within a single, predictive effective theory framework based on Froggatt-Nielsen mechanisms.
AI.method: Extends Froggatt-Nielsen framework with three right-handed neutrinos for Type-I seesaw mechanism, incorporates complex FN coefficients for CP violation, uses lightest RHN as dark matter candidate, and computes CP asymmetries from RHN decays including flavon-mediated processes for leptogenesis.
AI.result: Shows that successful thermal leptogenesis can be achieved in both freeze-in and freeze-out DM production regimes, with large-vφ region approaching standard leptogenesis limits and low-vφ region requiring resonant enhancement due to lighter RHNs.
AI.conclusion: The constrained framework provides a unified description where the FN symmetry-breaking scale vφ simultaneously controls RHN masses and flavon/DM sector interactions, offering predictive connections between flavor physics, neutrino physics, dark matter, and baryogenesis.

title: 7D (non-)susy vacua & DWs from dynamical open strings
summary: Warped compactifications of massive type IIA supergravity on a 3-sphere with spacetime-filling O6/D6 sources are known to admit a half-maximal gauged supergravity description in 7D. We study the effect of introducing open string degrees of freedom (scalars and fluxes) in such dimensional reductions, associated with the spacetime-filling sources. From the 7D supergravity point of view, this can be realized by coupling the gravity multiplet with extra vector multiplets and adding new components to the embedding tensor describing the gauging. The scalar potential of the underlying theory exhibits novel AdS7 vacuum solutions, with and without supersymmetry. Finally, we explore the net of domain wall solutions interpolating between the different pairs of vacua, and present analytical as well as numerical solutions.

AI.tldr: Study of warped compactifications of massive type IIA supergravity on S³ with O6/D6 sources, incorporating open string degrees of freedom, leading to novel AdS₇ vacua and domain wall solutions.
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of including open string degrees of freedom (scalars and fluxes) associated with spacetime-filling O6/D6 sources in warped compactifications of massive type IIA supergravity, and to explore the resulting vacuum structure and domain wall solutions in the 7D supergravity description.
AI.method: Extend existing 7D half-maximal gauged supergravity description by coupling the gravity multiplet with extra vector multiplets and adding new components to the embedding tensor describing the gauging, incorporating open string degrees of freedom from spacetime-filling sources.
AI.result: The scalar potential exhibits novel AdS₇ vacuum solutions, both supersymmetric and non-supersymmetric. A network of domain wall solutions interpolating between different pairs of vacua is explored, with both analytical and numerical solutions presented.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating open string degrees of freedom from spacetime-filling sources in warped compactifications of massive type IIA supergravity leads to richer vacuum structure with novel AdS₇ solutions and domain wall interpolations, extending the landscape of 7D supergravity theories.

title: Accelerating Feynman Integral Evaluation by Avoiding Contour Deformation
comment: Contribution to the 17th International Symposium on Radiative Corrections: Applications of Quantum Field Theory to Phenomenology (RADCOR2025), 5-10 October 2025, Puri, India
summary: We describe our method for rewriting dimensionally regulated Feynman parameter integrals in the Minkowski regime as a sum of real, positive integrands multiplied by complex prefactors. This representation eliminates the need for a contour deformation, which is one of the main computational bottlenecks in numerical integration. We demonstrate clearly how the method works on two examples, and benchmark the performance against contour deformation as implemented in pySecDec, where we observe performance gains of up to several orders of magnitude. We describe an improvement in the resolution procedure using the Generic Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition algorithm, which generalises our method to any Feynman integral, including those with massive propagators.

AI.tldr: Method for rewriting dimensionally regulated Feynman parameter integrals in Minkowski regime as sum of real positive integrands with complex prefactors, eliminating need for contour deformation and achieving significant performance gains.
AI.motivation: Contour deformation is a major computational bottleneck in numerical integration of Feynman integrals in the Minkowski regime. The paper aims to develop a more efficient alternative that avoids this computationally expensive step.
AI.method: Rewrites dimensionally regulated Feynman parameter integrals as a sum of real, positive integrands multiplied by complex prefactors. Uses Generic Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition algorithm to improve resolution procedure, enabling generalization to any Feynman integral including those with massive propagators.
AI.result: Demonstrates method on two examples and benchmarks against contour deformation implementation in pySecDec. Observes performance gains of up to several orders of magnitude compared to contour deformation approach.
AI.conclusion: The method provides an efficient alternative to contour deformation for numerical integration of Feynman integrals in Minkowski regime, with significant performance improvements and generalization to arbitrary Feynman integrals including massive cases.

title: Scattering amplitudes in dimensionless quadratic gravity coupled to QED
summary: We study ultra-Planckian $2\to2$ scattering in an Abelian gauge theory coupled to agravity, the scale-free and renormalizable realization of quadratic quantum gravity. Focusing on charged fermions and scalars interacting with the photon and the higher-derivative graviton, we present compact analytic expressions for the unpolarized squared matrix elements for a broad set of tree-level processes, including photon--photon, fermion--fermion, fermion--photon, scalar--fermion, scalar--photon, scalar--scalar, and annihilation channels. In contrast to purely graviton-mediated analyses, we retain systematically the photon--graviton interference contributions and verify explicitly the independence of the results on the gravitational gauge-fixing parameter. The amplitudes display characteristic forward/backward enhancements associated with small momentum transfer, amplified by the $1/p^{4}$ graviton propagator, while their high-energy scaling reflects the underlying dimensionless gravitational couplings. Moreover, for all channels analyzed the corresponding differential cross sections exhibit the universal ultra-Planckian scaling $dσ/dΩ\propto 1/s$, where $s$ is the Mandelstam invariant (the squared center-of-momentum energy). Our results furnish a unified amplitude-level description of how higher-derivative gravity reshapes familiar QED scattering at ultra-Planckian energies and provide analytic building blocks for further studies of IR definitions and UV consistency in agravity with matter.

AI.tldr: Study of ultra-Planckian 2→2 scattering in Abelian gauge theory coupled to agravity (scale-free quadratic quantum gravity), providing analytic expressions for various tree-level processes with photon-graviton interference.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-derivative gravity (agravity) modifies familiar QED scattering at ultra-Planckian energies, and to provide analytic building blocks for studying IR definitions and UV consistency in agravity with matter.
AI.method: Focus on charged fermions and scalars interacting with photon and higher-derivative graviton; compute unpolarized squared matrix elements for tree-level processes including photon-photon, fermion-fermion, fermion-photon, scalar-fermion, scalar-photon, scalar-scalar, and annihilation channels; systematically retain photon-graviton interference contributions; verify gauge-fixing independence.
AI.result: Amplitudes show forward/backward enhancements from small momentum transfer amplified by 1/p⁴ graviton propagator; high-energy scaling reflects dimensionless gravitational couplings; all channels exhibit universal ultra-Planckian scaling dσ/dΩ ∝ 1/s (where s is squared center-of-momentum energy).
AI.conclusion: Results provide unified amplitude-level description of how higher-derivative gravity reshapes QED scattering at ultra-Planckian energies, offering analytic building blocks for further studies of IR definitions and UV consistency in agravity with matter.
